FAN_A0.prompt: A letter! Then you'll want a claim to write home about.

opening.speaker: fanshawe
opening.line: Mr. Grubb! Off the coach this morning and in my office by noon. You'll want a claim. Everyone wants a claim.

opening.speaker: thad
opening.line: I have come about a letter.

opening.speaker: fanshawe
opening.line: A letter! Then you'll want a claim to write home about.

options.text: I'm looking for Ezra Pike.
options.say: Dear Ezra. He has moved somewhere very quiet. The undertaker keeps his address.

options.text: I don't want a claim.
options.say: Nobody does on the first day. On the second they've bought one, and on the third they come to me. I'll keep the chair warm.

options.text: I have four dollars.
options.say: Then you are the best-capitalized man to arrive this week, and I congratulate you, and I would keep a hand on them in the Nugget.

options.text: Is it always this warm in here?
options.say: Always. I keep a fire in every season. Warm men are generous men, Mr. Grubb, and so are warm offices.

options.text: I should go.

FAN_A1.prompt: Everyone here has. It's how we get our start. Which claim?

opening.speaker: fanshawe
opening.line: Mr. Grubb! Sit down, sit down. You've the look of a man who's been sold something.

opening.speaker: fanshawe
opening.line: Everyone here has. It's how we get our start. Which claim?

options.text: Number two. Prosperity.
options.say: Prosperity! You've named it. Nobody names them. I like you enormously.

options.text: I'd rather not say.
options.say: Very wise. Very wise indeed.

options.text: Were you really a colonel?
options.say: Chapultepec, '47. Terrible business. Wonderful weather.

options.text: You have a great many chairs.
options.say: I do! I have found that a man will tell you anything if you sit him down. It's the standing ones you want to watch.

options.text: I've taken enough of your time. I'll be taking more later.

FAN_A2.prompt: You'll take wine. It takes itself, mostly.

opening.speaker: fanshawe
opening.line: You'll take wine. It takes itself, mostly.

options.text: I'd be glad of a partner in it.
options.say: Partners! Then we are partners. We'll do the paper when we're sober. I never do paper in drink. It's the only rule I keep.

options.text: You're welcome to the working of it while I learn the trade.
options.say: A lease! How modern of you. I'll have Sump draw something up.

options.text: Whatever's in it, I'd sooner it went to someone who'd use it.
options.say: Then we agree entirely, and that is the best foundation for anything. More wine?

options.text: Put it down as a kindness, and I'll owe you.

exchange.speaker: fanshawe
exchange.line: You owe me nothing at all, Mr. Grubb.

options.text: I'd sign anything that came with a wine like this.
options.say: Then you shall sign nothing tonight. I would never take advantage of a man at his dinner.

options.text: I mean to work it myself.
This is very good wine.
options.say: Isn't it! I have no idea what it is. I buy whatever costs most and let it explain itself.

options.text: I am going to leave now, in a dignified manner.
options.say: Already? Then come back when you're hungry. The table will keep.

FAN_B1.prompt: Sump! A dear friend. I shall write you a note. Sump respects notes the way other men respect weather.

opening.speaker: fanshawe
opening.line: Sump! A dear friend. I shall write you a note. Sump respects notes the way other men respect weather.

options.text: I need to see the Registrar about my boundary.
options.say: Your boundary! A man who knows where he ends. Rare. I shall send a note ahead.

options.text: What do you want for it?
options.say: Want? Mr. Grubb, a favor that costs something is a transaction. I deal only in favours.

options.text: Your clock is slow.
options.say: It is eleven minutes slow, and it has made me the most punctual man in the territory. Everyone else trusts it.

options.text: Thank you. This has been clarifying.

FAN_B2.prompt: The famous card! Take a copy. Take two. History belongs to everybody.

opening.speaker: fanshawe
opening.line: The famous card! Take a copy. Take two. History belongs to everybody.

options.text: I'd like to see Claim One's index card.
options.say: Of course. You'll find it agrees with the sealed filing in every particular.

options.text: Why does the Company keep copies of claim records?
options.say: Because the courthouse could burn down, Mr. Grubb. Buildings do.

options.text: Buena Vista must have been something.
options.say: Buena Vista! Spring of '48. I shall never forget it.

options.text: The chairs are new.
options.say: They are! One must reinvest.

options.text: I should go.
May I read the contract?

exchange.speaker: fanshawe
exchange.line: Of course! Read every word. I want you to read every word.

exchange.speaker: thad
exchange.line: He doesn't want the claim. He wants it quiet.

options.text: Yes.

exchange.speaker: fanshawe
exchange.line: Ink! The one thing this office never has. Forgive me — I'll send for some.

options.text: No.
options.say: Twelve thousand.

repeats.say: Fourteen, and you drive a very hard bargain for a man who isn't bargaining.

options.text: Why does a worthless claim cost eleven thousand dollars?
options.say: Because you'd like it to be worth more, and I'd like you to be happy.

options.text: I've named a raccoon after you.
options.say: Have you! What a splendid animal it must be.

options.text: I've taken enough of your time. I'll be taking more later.
